A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMPACT and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments and relocated material can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training evaluations across eight main benchmarks, ablations, dataset analyses, and additional knowledge-intensive benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, controlled complexity experiments, token and failure analyses, and an open-source generator evaluation.

M1.justification: The four-step recipe, atomic taxonomy, and trained model remain. However, v1 explicitly rejects questions requiring extra capabilities, whereas v2 describes the sampled count k_gen as a lower bound on actual complexity. Its appendix still requires exactly k capabilities. The PDFs do not establish whether verification changed or its behavior was reinterpreted.

E1.justification: Both use LLaVA-665K images and the same eight main benchmarks. OK-VQA, MMMU, and MMMU-Pro are retained from v1 Table 4 in v2 Figure 9. New complexity breakdowns and generator experiments remain within this existing task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands beyond full LLaVA-665K, Random, and ICONS by adding evaluated 65K-data comparisons with EL2N, Perplexity, SemDeDup, D2-Pruning, Self-Sup, and Self-Filter. This substantially broadens the comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds k+0/k+1 regeneration controls, two additional complexity-range settings, TextVQA stratification, and a Qwen3 generator configuration. The distribution-matched control now matches capability and k distributions. LLaVA complexity analysis changes from 5,668 to 5,400 questions, and its annotation prompt replaces object relationship with scene understanding. The main one-epoch LLaVA training setup remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled complexity augmentation, TextVQA difficulty analysis, MMStar category and complexity breakdowns, capability correlations, token efficiency, generation failures, and generator robustness analyses. It removes v1's direct COMPACT-versus-full-VIT high-k analysis in Figure 4. The leave-one-capability-out analysis is retained as Table 7, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v2 Table 8 newly reports token-length means with ± terms, without defining the spread statistic. The complexity-range display also drops v1 Figure 7's unexplained shaded bands. Neither version documents repeated-training uncertainty or evaluation seeds; v2's average three runs per question concerns data generation.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 rows are unchanged, but added results change rankings: EL2N scores 33.53 on MM-Vet versus COMPACT's 31.74, and D2-Pruning scores 36.63 on MMStar versus 36.13. Table 3 replaces the 96.62% unbalanced-control result with 97.55% under revised matching conditions. New Qwen3 results reach 98.31% relative performance. Complexity estimates and supplementary findings also change, while v1's direct high-k generalization results disappear.

T1.justification: Both retain complexity k as the number of required atomic capabilities. v2 introduces a distinct sampled count k_gen and explicitly states k_gen ≤ k, replacing v1's identification of requested and realized complexity. This is a limited revision to the mathematical characterization; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on balanced exact-k training and generalization beyond trained complexity levels. v2 reframes the contribution around informative synthetic questions and complexity-aware data efficiency, dropping the headline unseen-complexity gains. Matching full-data performance with approximately 10% of the data remains a central claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains implicit object recognition and overlapping capabilities, qualifies the taxonomy as a practical choice, and discusses tradeoffs between simple and complex training examples. Revised Table 3 supports attributing roughly half the gain to complexity, replacing v1's 'most' interpretation. Appendix A.6 adds substantive remaining failure conditions, including incorrect answers and ambiguous spatial or occluded attributes.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies generation temperature 0.1, top-p 0.9, a 1,000-token limit, average generation runs, 32 parallel processes, approximately two hours, and $86.5 cost. These are useful disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing settings. The project URL and promise of a future data release remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions COMPACT around data curation and complexity-controlled efficiency. It adds the six data-reduction baseline works and a compositional visual reasoning survey, while removing several compositionality and diagnostic references, including Fodor and LePore and Zhao et al. Taxonomy provenance shifts from benchmark literature toward LLaVA data curation and manual inspection.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, interpretation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around information density and complexity-aware curation. Analyses are reorganized between the main text and appendix, which gains numbered subsections and a contents page. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout and extensively redesigns displays. Figure 1 becomes an experimental comparison; capability heatmaps become frequency bars; the capability ablation becomes a table; complexity-range curves become heatmaps; and the instruction-ratio plot shows separate benchmarks. New analytical displays and revised sample illustrations further change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for the data-efficiency contribution through broader baselines, regeneration controls, and an open-source generator test. It also replaces the strict unseen-complexity framing with a more qualified account and documents generation failures and settings. These gains outweigh remaining exact-k prompt inconsistencies and newly erroneous example answers in Figure 12, although those defects still weaken clarity and confidence in the illustrations.
